business: Headroom (UK software that finds revenue leakage for MSPs)
target: Owners and commercial leads of UK managed service providers (IT support businesses, 5 to 50 staff) that run clients' IT on monthly agreements

segments.name: Owner of a small UK MSP (5 to 10 staff, roughly £400k to £1m revenue)
Owner of a mid-sized UK MSP (11 to 30 staff, roughly £1m to £3m revenue)
Owner or commercial director of a larger UK MSP (31 to 50 staff, roughly £3m to £5m revenue)

behaviours.name: Ex-technician owner
behaviours.how: Still on the tools some days, does month-end billing personally in the PSA and a spreadsheet, rarely buys new software.

behaviours.name: Numbers-driven owner
behaviours.how: Has an accountant or finance person, watches margin per client, will pay for anything that shows a clear return.

behaviours.name: Burned by dashboards
behaviours.how: Has bought a BI or reporting tool before that took weeks to set up and then nobody looked at it.

behaviours.name: Already has a billing or BI tool
behaviours.how: Pays for a billing reconciliation or BI product (e.g. Gradient, MSPbots, BrightGauge) and sees new tools as overlap.

behaviours.name: Peer-group member
behaviours.how: Belongs to an MSP peer group, acts on benchmarks and what other owners recommend.

behaviours.name: Relationship-first
behaviours.how: Long-standing clients, hates awkward money conversations, often does small extra jobs for free to keep goodwill.

behaviours.name: Time-poor and growing
behaviours.how: Hiring and onboarding clients, buys things that save time, ignores anything that needs an afternoon of setup.

objections: Exporting all that data from my PSA and billing system is an afternoon I don't have
I'm not uploading my clients' ticket data to a company I've never heard of
My PSA reports already show me which agreements lose money
I already know we do some free work; that's how we keep clients
It will find money once, then what am I paying for every month?
Potential leakage isn't money in the bank; I'd have to chase every client
The numbers will be wrong because our ticket categories are messy
No integrations, no reviews, no customers yet
habits: you use ConnectWise PSA and QuickBooks
you raise invoices at month end and it always takes longer than it should
you run quarterly business reviews with your bigger clients
you read r/msp and a couple of MSP LinkedIn groups
you have two clients who you suspect are underpaying for how much they use you
your contracts are a mix of old PDFs and a newer template
